name: Provenance-tagging / architectural defenses against indirect prompt injection: IPIGuard (Tool Dependency Graph, EMNLP 2025 Oral, arXiv:2508.15310), CausalArmor (causal-attribution guardrails, arXiv:2602.07918), and Parallax (cognitive-executive separation + Information Flow Control, arXiv:2604.12986).
kind: Three distinct research results, all agent-runtime defense ARCHITECTURES (not extraction tools or standards) evaluated primarily on the AgentDojo benchmark (and DoomArena/TauBench-Retail for CausalArmor). Grouped because all three formalize some notion of provenance/trust-tagging as the load-bearing mechanism, directly answering this project's `provenance_carrying` field.
maturity: IPIGuard: peer-reviewed, EMNLP 2025 Oral (a strong acceptance signal), code released (github.com/Greysahy/ipiguard). CausalArmor and Parallax: both 2026 preprints (arXiv:2602.xxxxx and 2604.xxxxx respectively), not yet confirmed peer-reviewed; Parallax includes a named implementation ('Shield') with enough engineering detail (ONNX runtime, purego bridge, ~50ms optimization roadmap) to suggest a working prototype rather than a purely theoretical proposal.
license: Not independently confirmed for any of the three beyond IPIGuard's public GitHub release (github.com/Greysahy/ipiguard, license terms not separately verified).
keeps_and_discards: None of the three is a content extractor -- they operate on AGENT DECISIONS, not page content. What each 'keeps' is a structural or causal boundary: IPIGuard keeps a pre-planned Tool Dependency Graph (TDG) built from ONLY trusted information before any untrusted tool output is read, discarding the agent's ability to freely restructure its own execution plan based on content encountered mid-task. CausalArmor keeps a structured context decomposition C_t = (U, H_t, S_t) -- user request, trusted system context, and isolated untrusted spans -- kept SEPARATE until the point of causal-attribution measurement, discarding the common practice of flattening all context into one undifferentiated prompt. Parallax keeps a hard architectural boundary between the reasoning/planning subsystem (treated as fully untrusted) and the executing subsystem (structurally unable to reason), discarding any defense that lives inside the same computational substrate as the threat.
structure_preserved: IPIGuard's TDG explicitly models tool-call DEPENDENCY structure (deterministic nodes with known arguments vs. pending nodes resolved only from prior trusted-path outputs), and further splits tools into Query (read-only) vs. Command (state-changing) types -- a structural distinction directly relevant to any actuator layer this project might build. CausalArmor preserves per-SPAN structure (individual untrusted content segments remain independently addressable/ablatable rather than merged into one blob). Parallax's Information Flow Control (IFC) preserves LABEL structure across arbitrary transformation chains -- a sensitivity tag assigned at data origin persists through 'subsequent operations' regardless of how many intermediate steps separate a read from a write, directly the kind of provenance persistence this project's own provenance_carrying field asks about.
interactive_elements: Not directly relevant to page-content interactivity, but structurally analogous: IPIGuard's Query-vs-Command tool typing is the agent-action equivalent of distinguishing read-only from state-changing INTERACTIVE elements on a page (a button that reveals more content vs. a button that submits a form/payment) -- the same read/write distinction this project might want to apply to its own captured interactive-element taxonomy.
interactive_state_fidelity: Not applicable -- none of the three concerns control-state fidelity; their unit of concern is tool-call/action legitimacy.
layout_awareness: None of the three reads or requires layout -- all three operate on structured text/tool-call representations (prompts, tool outputs, action proposals), consistent with this project's own no_layout_in_the_fold posture, though for a different reason (efficiency/architecture, not a stated privacy/structure-agnosticism principle).
javascript_required: Not applicable -- these are LLM-agent runtime defenses, not page-capture mechanisms.
evaluation_method: All three use CONTROLLED benchmark evaluation with attack-success-rate (ASR) as the primary metric, benign-task-utility as the cost metric, and latency as the overhead metric -- IPIGuard and CausalArmor both on AgentDojo (629 test cases across banking/Slack/travel/workspace domains, 97 tasks, 70 tools per CausalArmor's fuller description); Parallax uses a self-designed 'Assume-Compromise Evaluation' that BYPASSES the LLM entirely and injects tool calls directly into its validation layer (Shield) to test the architectural boundary under FULL agent compromise, plus a separate check of whether frontier models (Claude Sonnet, Claude Haiku, Llama 3.1 8B) in normal reasoning mode ever succeed at the same attacks (finding: 0% success, i.e. current model safety training already blocks naive attacks, which the authors argue makes assume-compromise testing NECESSARY rather than redundant, since that same safety training is precisely what adversaries target).
corpus_size_and_origins: IPIGuard: AgentDojo, 97 tasks across 4 domains (Workspace, Slack, Travel, Banking), 629 total test cases. CausalArmor: same AgentDojo suite (629 injection tasks, 4 agent types, 70 tools, 3 attack templates) PLUS DoomArena/TauBench-Retail (115 tasks, adaptive attackers with database access, conversational setting, 89.47% baseline ASR -- a notably harsher threat model than AgentDojo's). Parallax: a self-constructed 337-case suite (280 adversarial cases across 9 categories + 50 false-positive/legitimate-action controls), independent of AgentDojo -- meaning Parallax's numbers are NOT directly comparable to IPIGuard/CausalArmor's since they share no common benchmark.
reported_precision_recall: IPIGuard on AgentDojo (GPT-4o-mini, 'Important Instructions' attack template implied consistent with CausalArmor's framing): No-Defense ASR 13.16%, Spotlight defense 11.31%, Detector approach 4.43%, IPIGuard 0.69% -- with Average Benign Utility 67.01% (highest among compared defenses) and Average Utility Under Attack 58.77% (also highest), at roughly 2x token/time overhead versus undefended. CausalArmor on AgentDojo (same 'Important Instructions' template, denominator = the same benchmark): No-Defense 32.47% ASR / 53.61 benign utility / 1.00x latency; DRIFT 4.99% ASR / 50.58 utility / 4.67x latency; MELON 0.53% ASR / 49.48 utility / 2.21x latency; CausalArmor 0.62% ASR / 56.26 utility (HIGHEST of all compared, i.e. LEAST harmful to benign tasks) / 1.30x latency -- the paper's central claim is resolving the 'over-defense dilemma' (strong ASR reduction without the usual utility/latency cost). On a stronger backbone (Claude-4-Sonnet), No-Defense ASR drops to 2.32% already (frontier models are more resistant unassisted) and CausalArmor pushes it to 0.0% at 1.27x latency, utility 82.47% vs. 89.44% undefended baseline. Parallax (Assume-Compromise mode, denominator = 280 adversarial cases): default configuration blocks 98.9% (277/280) at 0% false-positive rate (of 50 legitimate-action controls); maximum-security configuration blocks 100% at a STEEP 36% false-positive rate -- an explicit, honestly reported precision/recall tradeoff curve rather than a single cherry-picked operating point.
independent_oracle: Parallax's Assume-Compromise methodology is the most independent oracle of the three: it does not trust the LLM's own behavior as ground truth at all, instead injecting adversarial tool calls DIRECTLY into the validation layer, bypassing any possibility that a cooperative/well-behaved LLM masks a weak architectural defense. IPIGuard and CausalArmor's oracle is the benchmark's own labeled attack-success criteria (AgentDojo's built-in checkers), independent of the defense mechanism itself but not independent of the benchmark designer's own assumptions about what constitutes a successful attack.
evidence_independence: All three are academic, non-vendor-affiliated as far as confirmed. IPIGuard's EMNLP 2025 Oral acceptance is the strongest external-validation signal among the three (peer review at a top NLP venue). CausalArmor and Parallax are both unreviewed preprints as of this research pass -- their self-reported numbers, while methodologically detailed and internally consistent (and Parallax in particular is unusually candid about its own failure modes and false-positive rates), have not yet been independently replicated by a third party.
page_archetype_coverage: Not applicable -- none operates over web page content archetypes; their 'domains' are agent-task domains (banking, Slack, travel, workspace), not page structural types.
script_and_locale_behaviour: Not addressed by any of the three.
leaks_outward: Not the primary concern of any of the three (they defend AGAINST malicious actions, including presumably exfiltration-shaped ones, but do not themselves leak data) -- Parallax's IFC mechanism is explicitly designed to CATCH exactly the kind of leak this project's markdown-exfiltration item (item 7) describes: 'if the agent attempts to write RESTRICTED-tagged content to a network endpoint, Shield detects the flow violation regardless of how many intermediate steps separate read from write' -- a direct architectural countermeasure to the read-then-exfiltrate pattern.
mechanism_detectability: Not applicable in the page-capture sense; Parallax does address a structurally analogous 'validator-targeted attack' category (attempts to read, modify, or exhaust the validation layer itself) as one of its seven named threat categories, and its Tier 2 LLM evaluator includes canary-token verification specifically to detect injection attempts targeting the EVALUATOR itself -- a defense-of-the-defense mechanism worth noting.
countermeasures: This field IS the subject of all three items; see reported_precision_recall and measured_fidelity_cost for the specific mechanisms and their measured effectiveness. Summarizing the three distinct architectural strategies: IPIGuard = pre-commit to a trusted execution plan (Tool Dependency Graph) before touching untrusted data, with a 'fake tool invocation' trick to satisfy injected instructions without ever really executing them; CausalArmor = measure causal attribution (leave-one-out ablation) at each privileged-action decision point and selectively sanitize only the untrusted span that dominates; Parallax = four-tier graduated-determinism validation (deterministic policy -> dual classifier -> budget-limited LLM evaluation with inverted context -> human approval) plus Information Flow Control tagging that survives arbitrary transformation chains.
measured_fidelity_cost: All three report this honestly and specifically (a notably strong property versus most items in this research set): IPIGuard costs ~2x token usage and task-completion time versus undefended. CausalArmor costs only 1.27-1.30x latency (its headline efficiency win) via 'Batched Proxy Attribution' -- routing leave-one-out ablation queries through a SMALLER proxy model (Gemma-3-12B-IT) rather than the frontier model itself, reducing 'interaction depth to O(1) sequential proxy invocations per decision point.' Parallax's tiered system has per-tier latency: Tier 0 <1ms, Tier 1 ~1947ms P50 (dominated by ONNX runtime overhead, a known and named optimization target), Tier 2 ~2089ms P50; and its false-positive rate is the most starkly reported tradeoff of the three -- 0% FP at 98.9% block rate (default config) vs. 36% FP at 100% block rate (maximum-security config), an explicit Pareto frontier rather than a single number.
gate_state_at_capture: Not applicable -- none of the three concerns page capture or gating.
determinism: IPIGuard's TDG-based execution is deterministic BY CONSTRUCTION for the trusted portion of the plan (topological traversal of a pre-committed graph), with controlled non-determinism only in the argument-estimation step. CausalArmor's causal-attribution measurement is deterministic given a fixed proxy model and fixed threshold tau (with an explicit LENGTH-NORMALIZATION step specifically to keep tau consistent across differently-sized tool calls, i.e. a designed-for determinism property). Parallax's Tier 0-1 are fully deterministic (rule/classifier-based); Tier 2's LLM evaluation is only as deterministic as its underlying model, mitigated by the inverted-context design (no conversation history/agent state) intended to reduce variance from irrelevant context.
determinism_across_versions: Not directly addressed by any of the three; CausalArmor's reliance on a specific proxy model (Gemma-3-12B-IT) introduces a version-pinning dependency the paper does not discuss the risk of; the paper does explicitly flag a related but distinct risk (see failure_modes: proxy-model-mismatch/adversarial-optimization-against-disclosed-proxy).
reproducibility: IPIGuard: high, code publicly released. CausalArmor and Parallax: not confirmed whether code/data are released; both provide enough methodological detail (formulas, thresholds, tier breakdowns) to be independently reimplementable in principle.
failure_modes: Unusually well self-documented across all three (a distinguishing strength of this item versus most others in this research set). IPIGuard: Node Expansion's conservative attack classification can produce false negatives that CONSTRAIN legitimate tool calls (an over-defense side effect); ablating Node Expansion + Fake Tool Invocation still left ASR at 3.18% (i.e. those two mechanisms account for the gap between 3.18% and the full system's 0.69%, not the TDG structure alone). CausalArmor: explicitly acknowledges a THEORETICAL split-context vulnerability -- an adversary could fragment instructions across multiple spans to dilute per-span attribution below the detection threshold -- though empirically 'attacks exhibit a causal bottleneck' concentrating influence at decisive moments in their tested benchmark, meaning the theoretical weakness has not yet been empirically exploited in their own tests; also names a proxy-model-mismatch risk (attacker could optimize against a disclosed proxy architecture, mitigated by keeping proxy details confidential or rotating them). Parallax: names SIX distinct limitations including classifier domain mismatch (DeBERTa trained on prompt-injection TEXT classification, not agent-ACTION safety, causing false positives on structured-but-benign payloads like file content/emails/HTTP bodies), coarse IFC tag granularity, Tier 1's ~1.9s latency bottleneck (with a named fix: native C API integration to reach sub-50ms), and most importantly an EXPLICIT, non-hedged admission that Reversible Execution 'cannot undo external side effects (sent emails, API calls to third parties)' -- local rollback only, a hard architectural boundary the authors state plainly rather than obscure.
failure_visibility: All three score well here relative to the rest of this research set: IPIGuard and CausalArmor report ablation-study numbers that isolate WHICH component contributes how much defense (rather than one opaque end-to-end number); Parallax goes furthest, publishing its FALSE POSITIVE RATE alongside its block rate at multiple operating points, and naming the exact three attacks that succeeded under its default configuration (both 'contextually ambiguous file deletions and HTTP POSTs' judged low-risk by the Tier 2 evaluator) rather than reporting only an aggregate success number.
scale_limits: Not a primary focus of any of the three, though Parallax's per-tier latency breakdown functions as an implicit scale/cost analysis (73.6% of blocked attacks resolved by the two CHEAPEST tiers -- Tier 0 sub-millisecond, Tier 1 ~2s -- meaning the expensive Tier 2/3 escalation path is invoked on only a minority of cases, a favorable cost distribution by design).
delta_cost_model: Not directly applicable -- none has an incremental-DOM-update concept; their unit of 'delta' is per-DECISION (per privileged action / per tool call), not per-page-change. CausalArmor's O(1)-per-decision-point batched-proxy-attribution claim is the closest analogue to an O(delta)-style efficiency argument in this cluster.
reanchoring_stability: Not applicable -- no DOM element identity concept in any of the three.
adversarial_exposure: This field is the direct subject of all three, and together they form the most complete answer in this research set to whether provenance-based defenses can generalize: Parallax's threat-model taxonomy (7 categories: direct injection, indirect injection [>55% of real-world incidents per the authors], multi-step 'salami slicing' context manipulation, tool-use chain attacks, encoding/obfuscation, multi-agent compromise, and validator-targeted attacks) is the most complete adversarial taxonomy surfaced anywhere in this research pass, and IPIGuard/CausalArmor's ASR numbers give concrete, if benchmark-specific, evidence that structural/causal defenses meaningfully outperform prompt-level guardrails against at least the AgentDojo attack family.
provenance_carrying: The single most directly relevant field for this item, answered concretely by all three at different granularities: Parallax's Information Flow Control (IFC) is the closest architectural analogue to this project's own trie-key-carries-provenance design -- sensitivity tags are 'assigned at the point of origin based on path rules, content patterns, and configurable policies... within the executor, preventing the agent from manipulating classifications of data it reads,' and these tags 'persist through subsequent operations' regardless of intermediate step count, explicitly modeled on Bell-LaPadula multi-level-security principles. CausalArmor's structured context decomposition C_t = (U, H_t, S_t) is a coarser, three-way provenance split (trusted user / trusted system / untrusted external) maintained specifically to enable selective, span-level intervention. IPIGuard's TDG implicitly carries provenance by construction (only trusted-planning-time information can create Deterministic Nodes; anything derived from untrusted tool output becomes a Pending Node subject to constrained resolution).
roundtrip_safety: Not directly applicable -- none of the three has a serialize/reparse concept; their closest analogue is CausalArmor's retroactive Chain-of-Thought MASKING (replacing assistant reasoning traces post-injection-detection with '[Reasoning redacted for security]' before re-generation), which is a form of state-rollback-to-a-known-good-point rather than a fixed-point check.
token_budget_and_ordering: Indirectly relevant via cost overhead: IPIGuard's ~2x token-usage cost and CausalArmor's proxy-model batching (explicitly designed to REDUCE per-decision token/interaction cost versus naive sequential frontier-model queries) both bear on token budget, though neither treats context ORDERING as a first-class defense variable the way this project's own token_budget_and_ordering field does.
representation_cost: CausalArmor's proxy-model substitution (Gemma-3-12B-IT instead of the frontier backbone for ablation scoring) is a direct representation-cost optimization worth naming explicitly: it trades a small amount of attribution fidelity for a large reduction in per-decision compute cost, a pattern directly transferable to any expensive-oracle check this project might design.
what_could_be_adopted: Two mechanisms are strongly adoptable, one is adoptable-in-the-actuator-layer-only. STRONGLY ADOPTABLE: (1) Parallax's Information Flow Control pattern -- tag content by trust/sensitivity AT THE POINT OF CAPTURE (this project's trie/xpath-keyed provenance is already positioned to carry exactly this kind of tag) and propagate it through any downstream transform, checking for policy violations (e.g. untrusted-origin content flowing into a privileged sink) regardless of how many transformation steps intervene -- this is close to a direct match for the project's stated architecture and the single highest-value idea in this item. (2) IPIGuard's read-only-vs-state-changing (Query vs. Command) tool/action typing, applicable to this project's own interactive-element taxonomy if an actuator layer is ever built on top of the capture pipeline: classify captured controls by whether ACTING on them can only observe (safe to auto-explore) versus mutate state (requires elevated scrutiny), independent of any layout or region heuristic. ADOPTABLE IN THE ACTUATOR LAYER ONLY: CausalArmor's causal-attribution/dominance-shift detection and Parallax's tiered graduated-determinism validator are both AGENT-DECISION-TIME mechanisms that presuppose an agent already acting on captured content -- not applicable to the capture/fold layer itself, but directly relevant blueprints for any future actuator this project builds on top of its own captures.
constraint_violation_ledger: structure_agnosticism: ADOPTABLE AS-IS for all three -- none classifies PAGE regions (nav/article/result); their structural concerns are tool-call graphs and context spans, an entirely different structural axis that does not conflict with this constraint. no_layout_in_the_fold: ADOPTABLE AS-IS -- none of the three reads rendered geometry; all operate on structured text/tool-call representations. o_delta: NOT DIRECTLY APPLICABLE, BUT CONCEPTUALLY ALIGNED -- none has an incremental-DOM-update cost model, but CausalArmor's O(1)-per-decision-point design and Parallax's tiered escalation (cheapest checks first, most cases resolved cheaply) are both instances of the SAME amortization discipline O(delta) requires, applied to a different resource (agent-decision compute rather than ingest compute). no_mocks: ADOPTABLE AS-IS, WITH PARALLAX AS THE STRONGEST EXEMPLAR -- Parallax's Assume-Compromise methodology (bypassing the LLM to test the architectural boundary directly, rather than trusting a well-behaved model's own reported behavior) is itself a no-mocks-style discipline: it refuses to let a cooperative test subject stand in for a genuinely adversarial one, a directly transferable testing PHILOSOPHY for this project's own reliability claims. closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: NOT APPLICABLE -- orthogonal to shadow-DOM capture policy. OVERALL VERDICT: adoptable as-is at the PROVENANCE-TAGGING-MECHANISM level (Parallax's IFC is the closest architectural fit and the strongest single import candidate in this entire research pass for the project's provenance_carrying field), adoptable in the actuator layer only for the decision-time validation logic (CausalArmor, Parallax's Shield tiers, IPIGuard's TDG), and Parallax's Assume-Compromise testing philosophy is independently adoptable as a NO-MOCKS-COMPLIANT reliability-testing methodology regardless of whether any of the three architectures themselves are adopted.
governance_signal_handling: Not addressed by any of the three -- orthogonal to their scope.
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: Not addressed by any of the three directly, though Parallax's IFC mechanism (tagging content as e.g. RESTRICTED at origin and tracking its flow) is STRUCTURALLY the same mechanism a PII-handling policy would need -- the paper frames it around credential/security sensitivity rather than PII/lawful-basis specifically, but the underlying tag-and-track architecture is directly reusable for that purpose if this project needed it.
uncertain: Whether CausalArmor and Parallax have undergone or are undergoing peer review was not confirmed -- both are treated as preprints of unconfirmed review status as of this research pass
Exact code/data release status for CausalArmor and Parallax was not confirmed (only IPIGuard's GitHub release was directly verified)

CausalArmor's theoretical guarantee (Pr(Attack Success) <= T*|Y_mal|*exp(-(beta+gamma))) depends on two assumptions (backbone capability beta > 0, sanitization margin gamma > 0) whose real-world satisfiability was not independently verified beyond the paper's own stated framing

Parallax's 337-case test suite, while methodologically detailed, is self-constructed by the paper's own authors rather than a shared community benchmark like AgentDojo, so its numbers are not directly cross-comparable to IPIGuard/CausalArmor's AgentDojo-based figures despite superficially similar percentage formats
